q: Which source contains Florida's real estate license law?
ex: Chapter 475 F.S. is the real estate license law passed by the Legislature. Chapter 455 covers all DBPR professions generally; 61J2 contains FREC's rules made under Chapter 475.

1: Chapter 455 is the general law for all DBPR-regulated professions, not the real estate license law.
2: 61J2 is FREC's administrative rule chapter, adopted under the authority of Chapter 475.
3: The Fair Housing Act is federal anti-discrimination law.

q: The rule that a broker must deposit escrow funds by the end of the third business day is found in a rule adopted by the FREC. What kind of law is this?
ex: Rules adopted by an agency (here the FREC, in Chapter 61J2 F.A.C.) are administrative rules. They carry the force of law but must stay within the statute that authorizes them.

0: Escrow deadlines for Florida brokers are state rules, not federal statutes.
2: Court decisions interpret law; they do not set escrow deadlines.
3: The Florida Constitution does not contain escrow rules.

q: A licensee is accused of stealing escrow money. Which of the following can impose a prison sentence?
ex: Only a court can impose criminal penalties such as imprisonment. The FREC imposes administrative discipline (fines, suspension, revocation); the DBPR investigates.

0: The FREC disciplines the license but cannot imprison anyone.
1: The DBPR investigates and administers; it cannot imprison.
3: The probable cause panel only decides whether to file a formal complaint.

q: In Florida, a seller who knows of a hidden defect that materially affects the value of a home must disclose it to the buyer. The original source of this duty is:
c: Rule Chapter 61J2 of the Florida Administrative Code
A Florida Supreme Court decision, Johnson v. Davis
The federal Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act
The Florida Realtors/Florida Bar contract form
ex: Johnson v. Davis (Fla. 1985) created the seller's duty to disclose known latent defects materially affecting value. It is case law. The contract forms reflect it but did not create it.

0: 61J2 regulates licensees' conduct; the seller's disclosure duty comes from case law.
2: RESPA governs settlement procedures and kickbacks for federally related loans.
3: Contract forms reflect the duty; a disclosure duty exists even without a form.

q: Which statement about the term REALTOR® is correct?
c: It is the official title on a Florida sales associate license
It identifies a member of the National Association of REALTORS®
Every Florida broker must use it
It is issued by the FREC after the broker exam
ex: REALTOR® is a trademark identifying NAR members who subscribe to its Code of Ethics. Florida licenses are 'sales associate' and 'broker'.

0: The license title is 'sales associate'; REALTOR® is a trade-association membership mark.
3: The FREC issues nothing related to the trademark.

q: A church, a school and a hospital are best classified as which category of property?
ex: Properties with a unique, limited use such as churches, schools and hospitals are special-purpose properties.

3: Mixed-use combines residential and commercial uses.

q: A licensee who leases units, collects rents and arranges maintenance for an owner is working in which specialty?
ex: Property management covers leasing, rent collection and maintenance on behalf of owners.

3: Counseling is giving real estate advice for a fee.

q: A Florida real estate license is required when a person performs a real estate service:
c: for compensation, even on their own property
for another, even without any compensation
only if the person advertises to the public
ex: All three elements are needed: a real estate service, for another, for compensation (paid, promised or expected). Remove any one and no license is needed.

0: Owners dealing with their own property are exempt.
2: Without compensation (or the expectation of it) no license is required.
3: Advertising is one service, but the test is service + for another + compensation.

q: Marco, unlicensed, finds a buyer for his neighbour's house. The neighbour promises Marco a used car 'if the deal closes'. The deal closes and Marco receives the car. Which is correct?
c: No license was needed, because compensation means a payment of money
No license was needed, because a single favour for a neighbour is exempt
Marco violated the law by performing a real estate service for compensation
Only the neighbour violated the law, by paying an unlicensed person
ex: Compensation means anything of value, including a car. Marco found a buyer (a real estate service) for another for compensation. One-time activity is not an exemption.

0: Compensation includes anything of value, not just money.
1: There is no 'one-time favour' exemption when compensation is paid.
3: Marco is the one who performed services without a license.

q: Which activity is a real estate service under Chapter 475?
c: Painting a house before it is listed
Leasing a property for another for a fee
Inspecting a roof for a buyer
Lending money secured by a mortgage
ex: Leasing for another for compensation is a listed service (A BAR SALE: Advertise, Buy, Appraise, Rent, Sell, Auction, Lease, Exchange).

0: Painting is construction work, not a brokerage service.
2: Home inspection is a separate licensed profession.

q: A builder pays Sofia a fixed salary to sell homes in its subdivision. The builder then changes her pay to $1,000 for each home that closes. What is the effect?
c: She remains exempt because she works for the owner
She now needs a real estate license
She needs a license only if she sells more than 10 homes a year
She may continue if the builder holds a broker license
ex: Salaried employees of an owner can be exempt, but commissions or per-transaction pay remove the exemption. Paid per closing, she is performing services for compensation tied to transactions and needs a license.

0: The owner's-employee exemption depends on salary, not commission.
3: Even working for a broker, she would need her own license.

q: Which person is exempt from real estate licensure under s. 475.011?
c: A property manager paid 8% of collected rents to manage homes for several different owners
A salaried employee of the owner who leases units from the apartment community's onsite office
An unlicensed assistant whom the broker pays $200 for each showing she conducts for buyers
A friend of the broker who receives a referral fee each time she sends a buyer to the brokerage
ex: s. 475.011 exempts salaried employees of an owner (or of a broker for an owner) of an apartment community working in an onsite rental office in a leasing capacity.

0: Managing property for several owners for a percentage of rents requires a license.
2: Per-showing pay for real estate services requires a license.
3: Paying an unlicensed person for referrals of real estate business is not allowed.

q: An attorney at law handles a client's closing and also negotiates the sale of the client's property, charging a 3% commission on the price. Which is correct?
c: Exempt, because attorneys at law are always exempt from Chapter 475
Exempt, because the commission was earned while handling the closing
Not exempt: earning a brokerage commission requires a real estate license
Exempt, as long as the attorney is a member in good standing of The Florida Bar
ex: Attorneys are exempt when acting within their legal duties. Charging a commission for brokerage services takes the attorney outside that exemption.

0: The exemption covers legal services, not brokerage for a commission.
1: Handling the closing does not cover earning a sales commission.
3: Bar membership is what makes them a lawyer; it does not authorize brokerage commissions.

q: Under s. 475.011, an attorney in fact (holding a power of attorney) is exempt when:
c: acting only to execute contracts or conveyances for the owner
selling the owner's properties in exchange for a commission
advertising and negotiating the sale of the owner's property for a fee
managing the owner's rentals for a percentage of the rents collected
ex: The statute exempts attorneys in fact acting to execute contracts or conveyances only. Brokerage activity for compensation is not covered.

1: Earning commissions is brokerage, not signing on the owner's behalf.
2: Advertising for several owners for pay is a real estate service.
3: Property management for a percentage requires a license.

q: Which is NOT a requirement to apply for a Florida sales associate license?
c: A high school diploma or its equivalent
ex: Florida residency and U.S. citizenship are not required. Applicants must be 18+, have a high school diploma or equivalent, and a Social Security number.

1: A diploma or equivalent is required.
2: A Social Security number is required.

q: A student completed the 63-hour pre-license course 26 months ago and has not taken the state exam. What is the status of the course for exam purposes?
c: Still valid — course completion never expires for exam purposes
Expired — it is valid for 2 years for purposes of the state exam
Still valid — course completion is valid for 3 years for the exam
Still valid — it remains valid until the student takes the exam
ex: Pre-license course completion is valid for 2 years for purposes of taking the state exam. At 26 months it has expired.

0: Course completion is valid for 2 years.
3: It expires after 2 years whether or not the exam has been taken.

q: An applicant with a 7-year-old misdemeanor conviction answers 'No' to the criminal-history question. Which is the most accurate consequence?
c: No consequence, because misdemeanors older than five years need not be disclosed
The false answer is itself grounds for denial or revocation and may be a crime
No consequence, because the FREC cannot consider any record older than 5 years
No consequence, because only felony convictions must be disclosed on applications
ex: Criminal history must be disclosed. An old record does not automatically disqualify, but a false answer on the application is grounds for denial or revocation and is itself a crime.

0: Criminal history, including misdemeanors, must be disclosed.
2: There is no 5-year rule; the FREC weighs the record and the applicant's honesty.
3: Misdemeanors can also be considered; honesty is the issue.

q: Lucas holds an active license in a state with a Florida mutual recognition agreement. He moved to Orlando last year and now wants a Florida license through mutual recognition. Which is correct?
c: He may use mutual recognition and must pass a 40-question law exam
He cannot use mutual recognition because he is a Florida resident when applying
He must take only the 63-hour course
He may practice in Florida immediately under his home-state license
ex: Mutual recognition is only for applicants who are NOT Florida residents at the time of application. As a resident, Lucas must follow the normal path (63-hour course and state exam).

0: The 40-question exam path is only for nonresidents.
2: Residents must complete the course AND pass the state exam.
3: No out-of-state license authorizes practice in Florida.

q: A nonresident licensee applying under mutual recognition must pass a Florida law exam of:
ex: The mutual recognition exam is 40 questions on Florida law; 30 correct (75%) passes.

0: 100/75 is the full sales associate exam.
2: It is 40 questions with 30 to pass.

q: How many members of the FREC must be licensed brokers who have held active licenses for the preceding 5 years?
ex: Four members must be brokers active for the 5 preceding years; one is a broker or sales associate active for 2 years; two are consumer members who have never been licensed.

0: 2 is the number of consumer members.
3: 5 is the years of experience, not the number of members.

q: Which statement about FREC membership is correct?
c: Members are elected by Florida licensees at the annual meeting, for 2-year terms
Members are appointed by the Governor, confirmed by the Senate, for 4-year terms
Members are appointed by the DBPR Secretary and serve until they choose to resign
Members are appointed by the Governor, and all seven must be licensed brokers
ex: The Governor appoints FREC members, subject to Senate confirmation, for 4-year terms. Two members are consumers who have never held a license.

0: Members are appointed, not elected, and terms are 4 years.
2: The Governor appoints; terms are 4 years.
3: Two members must never have been licensed.

q: When the FREC adopts a rule setting advertising requirements, it is exercising which power?
ex: Rule-making is quasi-legislative. Deciding discipline cases is quasi-judicial.

0: Quasi-judicial is deciding cases and imposing discipline.
2: Executive/administrative functions (licensing, records) are mostly DBPR's.
3: Prosecution is done by DBPR attorneys (discipline) or state attorneys (crimes); adopting rules is not prosecution.

q: A buyer files a complaint against a sales associate. Which body investigates it?
ex: The DBPR receives and investigates complaints. The FREC (through a probable cause panel and final orders) decides discipline.

0: The FREC decides discipline; it does not investigate.

q: A person holds a broker license but works under another broker's supervision. This person is a:
ex: A broker associate holds a broker license but operates as an associate under another broker.

0: A sales associate holds a sales associate license.
2: Transaction broker is a brokerage relationship, not a license type.
3: Designated sales associate is a role in certain nonresidential deals.

q: To qualify for a broker license, a sales associate must have held an active license for at least:
ex: 24 months of active sales associate licensure during the preceding 5 years, then the 72-hour broker course and broker exam.

q: Which person may hold multiple licenses?
c: A sales associate working for two unrelated brokers
A broker who is a broker for two unconnected brokerages
A broker associate working for two brokers
A sales associate under a group license
ex: Only a broker may hold multiple licenses (for separate, unconnected brokerages). A sales associate can work for one employer at a time; a group license covers connected entities of one owner-developer.

0: A sales associate may work for only one employer at a time.
2: An associate works under one employer.
3: A group license is one license covering connected entities.

q: A sales associate fails to complete post-license education before the first renewal. The license:
ex: Missing the 45-hour post-license requirement makes the license null and void. Missing CE at a later renewal makes it involuntarily inactive.

0: Involuntary inactive is the result of missing a later renewal/CE.
3: The license does not remain active.

q: After the first renewal, a sales associate must complete how many hours of continuing education each renewal period?
ex: 14 hours of CE every 2-year renewal period after the first.

1: 28 hours is the reactivation course after more than 12 months of involuntary inactivity.

q: Rita's license has been involuntarily inactive for 18 months. What must she do to reactivate it?
c: Nothing yet; she may simply pay the renewal fee within 2 years
Complete the regular 14 hours of commission-prescribed CE
Retake the 63-hour pre-license course and pass the state exam
ex: More than 12 but fewer than 24 months involuntarily inactive: 28-hour reactivation course. 12 months or less: 14 hours. More than 24 months: the license expires.

0: She must complete education to reactivate.
1: 14 hours applies only if inactive 12 months or less.
3: Requalifying is required only after the license expires (more than 2 years).

q: Which license status can be renewed indefinitely without the holder working for a broker?
ex: A licensee may choose voluntary inactive status and keep renewing it (with CE) indefinitely. Involuntary inactive expires after 2 years.

2: Suspension is discipline for a set time.
3: A void license no longer exists.

q: A sales associate let her license lapse (involuntary inactive) 26 months ago. What is her status?
c: Null and void; she must requalify
Active once she pays the fee
ex: Involuntary inactive status lasts at most 2 years. After 26 months the license has expired (null and void).

0: The 28-hour course applies only between 12 and 24 months.
1: She did not choose voluntary status.
3: Paying a fee cannot revive an expired license.

q: A licensee changes her mailing address. Within how many days must she notify the DBPR?
ex: Address changes must be reported within 10 days. Convictions and pleas must be reported within 30 days.

3: 30 days is the deadline for reporting a conviction or plea.

q: A sales associate pleads nolo contendere to a misdemeanor and adjudication is withheld. What must she do?
c: Nothing, because she was not convicted
Report it at her next renewal
ex: Licensees must report a conviction, a guilty plea, or a plea of nolo contendere within 30 days, whether or not adjudication is withheld.

0: A nolo plea must be reported even without a conviction.

q: Tom's employing broker closes the office. While looking for a new broker, Tom keeps showing his clients' listings. Which is correct?
c: Lawful, because his license remains current and active until it expires
Lawful for up to 30 days while he registers with a new employing broker
Unlawful: his license is ineffective until registered with a new employer
Lawful, as long as each client consents in writing to his continued help
ex: A sales associate may act only under a registered employer. When employment ends, the license cannot be used until the new employer's registration is filed.

0: A current license is not enough; it must be registered with an employer.
3: Client consent cannot authorize unlicensed activity.

q: Unless a different relationship is established in writing, a Florida real estate licensee is presumed to be operating as a:
ex: Florida presumes a transaction-broker relationship unless a single agent or no brokerage relationship is established in writing.

0: Single agency must be established in writing.
1: Dual agency is illegal in Florida.
3: Subagency is not one of Florida's authorized relationships.

q: A brokerage is a single agent for a seller. The same brokerage's buyer customer wants to buy the property. How may the brokerage lawfully proceed?
c: Continue as single agent for the seller and also become single agent for the buyer
Act as a dual agent for both parties after both sign a written dual-agency consent
Obtain the seller's written consent to transition, then act as transaction broker for both
Refer the buyer to another brokerage, because Florida forbids working both sides
ex: A brokerage may not be a single agent for both sides. With the principal's prior written consent to transition, it may act as a transaction broker for both.

0: Single agency for both sides is dual agency, which Florida prohibits.
1: Consent does not legalize dual agency in Florida.
3: Florida provides a lawful path (transition to transaction broker).

q: In a transaction-broker relationship, the buyer is a:
ex: A transaction broker provides limited representation and is not a fiduciary; the party is a customer. Only a single agent has a principal.

0: Principal is the term for a single agent's client.
2: The licensee, not the buyer, would be the fiduciary in single agency.
3: Subagency is not an authorized Florida relationship.

q: Which duty is owed by a single agent but NOT by a transaction broker?
c: Presenting all offers and counteroffers in a timely manner
ex: Loyalty, obedience, full confidentiality and full disclosure belong only to the single agent. The other three choices are owed by transaction brokers too.

0: Honesty is owed in every relationship.
1: Accounting is owed in every relationship.
3: Presenting offers is a transaction-broker duty too.

q: How many duties does a licensee owe a party with whom there is NO brokerage relationship?
ex: No brokerage relationship: 3 duties (honesty, disclosure of known material facts on residential property, accounting). Transaction broker 7; single agent 9.

q: A seller tells her transaction broker she would accept $20,000 less than list price. The broker tells a buyer, hoping to close quickly. Which duty did the broker breach?
c: No duty, because transaction brokers are neutral
ex: Limited confidentiality forbids revealing that the seller will accept less than the asking price (unless waived in writing).

0: Loyalty is owed only by a single agent.
2: Obedience is owed only by a single agent.

q: Which is part of a transaction broker's duty of limited confidentiality?
c: Not disclosing that a buyer is willing to pay more than the offered price
Not disclosing known latent defects the seller asked to keep confidential
Not presenting low offers the seller has said she would find insulting
Not accounting to either party for deposits until the day of closing
ex: Limited confidentiality protects price flexibility, motivation and information a party asks to keep confidential. It never permits hiding material defects or withholding offers or funds.

1: Known material defects on residential property must be disclosed in every relationship.
2: All offers must be presented in a timely manner.
3: Funds must be accounted for at all times.

q: A seller instructs his single agent: 'Don't mention the foundation crack you saw.' What must the agent do?
c: Obey the instruction, because obedience is one of the single agent's duties
Disclose the known material defect; obedience covers lawful instructions only
Stay silent about the crack unless the buyer asks a direct question about it
Withdraw from the listing and keep the information confidential permanently
ex: Obedience is limited to lawful instructions. Disclosure of known facts materially affecting the value of residential property is owed in all relationships.

0: Obedience never covers an unlawful instruction.
2: The duty does not depend on the buyer asking.
3: Confidentiality does not cover concealing known material defects.

q: When must a Single Agent Notice be given?
c: At or before closing, together with the other closing documents the parties sign
Before or when a listing/representation agreement is signed, or before a showing, whichever is first
Within 24 hours after the first showing, or after a representation agreement is signed, if later
Only when the customer asks in writing which brokerage relationship applies
ex: The single agent notice must be given before or at the time of entering into a listing or representation agreement, or before showing property, whichever occurs first.

3: It is mandatory in residential sales.

q: Which brokerage relationship requires NO written disclosure in Florida?
ex: Transaction broker is the presumed relationship and requires no disclosure.

1: A No Brokerage Relationship Notice is required before showing.
3: Designated sales associates require signed disclosures.

q: In which transaction are Florida's brokerage relationship disclosure requirements applicable?
ex: Disclosures apply to residential sales: ≤4 units, unimproved land for ≤4 units, or agricultural property ≤10 acres. Leases (without an option to buy), 5+ units and auctions are outside.

0: Rentals and leases are excluded unless they include an option to purchase ≤4 units.

q: Which situation does NOT require a brokerage relationship disclosure?
c: Showing a buyer a single-family home after she called the office about the listing
Answering general questions at a bona fide open house, with no confidential or price talk
Taking an exclusive-right-of-sale listing on a duplex owned by two investors
Showing a buyer an unimproved lot that is zoned for one single-family home
ex: Bona fide open houses with no confidential information, offer, or representation agreement are exempt. The other choices are residential sales activities.

0: Showing residential property requires a disclosure (before showing).
3: Unimproved land intended for ≤4 units is residential.

q: The Consent to Transition to Transaction Broker must be signed by the principal:
c: at closing, along with all of the other transaction documents
before the licensee changes from single agent to transaction broker
only if the customer on the other side requests it in writing
within 10 days after the licensee begins acting as transaction broker
ex: The principal must consent in writing before the change from single agent to transaction broker.

2: It is the principal's consent, and it is required.
3: Consent must come before the change.

q: Which fact does Florida law declare NOT material, so a licensee need not disclose it?
c: The roof leaks during heavy rain
A homicide occurred in the house
ex: Florida law (s. 689.25) provides that a homicide, suicide or death on the property, and an occupant's HIV/AIDS status, are not material facts. Physical defects that affect value must be disclosed.

0: A hidden roof leak is a latent material defect.
2: A failing seawall materially affects value.

q: A broker may appoint designated sales associates for the buyer and the seller when:
c: the transaction is residential and both parties agree in writing to the arrangement
the deal is nonresidential and buyer and seller each have assets of $1 million or more
the sale price of the property, residential or commercial, exceeds $1 million
the broker or one of the sales associates owns an interest in the property
ex: Designated sales associates are available only in nonresidential transactions where both buyer and seller have assets of $1 million or more (and request it in writing).

2: The test is each party's assets, not the price.
3: Ownership by the broker is unrelated.

q: After a listing expires, a buyer asks the former listing broker what price the seller had said she would accept. The broker had been a single agent. Which is correct?
c: The broker may answer, because all duties ended when the listing expired
The broker must not answer; confidentiality survives the end of the relationship
The broker may answer if the buyer signs a buyer-brokerage agreement first
The broker must answer, because the duty of honesty requires full answers
ex: Confidentiality (and the duty to account) survives the end of the brokerage relationship.

3: Honesty does not require revealing a former principal's confidential information.

q: A seller in an 'AS IS' sale knows his Florida home's slab is cracked and the crack is hidden under carpet. Must he disclose it?
c: No, because an AS IS contract means the buyer accepts every defect
No, unless the buyer's home inspector discovers the crack during inspection
Yes, known hidden defects that materially affect value must be disclosed, AS IS or not
Only if the buyer uses FHA financing, which requires a full disclosure form
ex: Under Johnson v. Davis the seller must disclose known latent defects that materially affect value. An AS IS contract shifts repair obligations, not the disclosure duty.

0: AS IS does not cancel the duty to disclose known hidden defects.
1: The duty exists regardless of the inspection.

q: A sales associate receives an earnest money check on Thursday. There are no holidays. By when must the broker deposit it?
ex: The associate delivers it to the broker by end of the next business day (Friday). The broker deposits by the end of the third business day after the brokerage received it — the day of receipt does not count: Friday (1), Monday (2), Tuesday (3).

0: End of Friday is the associate's deadline to deliver to the broker.
3: Counting the weekend or the day of receipt gives the wrong day; Tuesday is business day 3.

q: How much of the broker's own money may be kept in a sales escrow account to cover bank charges?
ex: Up to $1,000 in a sales escrow account; up to $5,000 in a property management escrow account. More is commingling.

3: A limited amount is allowed for bank charges.

q: A broker uses $3,000 from the escrow account to pay the office rent, planning to put it back next week. This is:
c: a minor violation subject only to a notice of noncompliance
ex: Using escrow funds for personal or business purposes is conversion — more serious than commingling (merely mixing funds).

0: Commingling is mixing funds; spending them is conversion.
2: There is no repayment grace period.
3: Misuse of trust funds is serious misconduct.

q: A broker may place escrow funds in an interest-bearing account only if:
c: the broker discloses that the brokerage will keep all of the interest
all parties consent in writing (including who receives the interest)
the deposit exceeds $10,000 and will be held for more than 30 days
the FREC approves the bank and the account in advance, in writing
ex: Interest-bearing escrow accounts require written consent of all parties, which also states who gets the interest.

0: The broker may not unilaterally keep the interest.
3: FREC approval is not the requirement.

q: After receiving conflicting demands for an escrow deposit, a broker must notify the FREC in writing within:
ex: Notice within 15 business days of the last demand; a settlement procedure must be instituted within 30 business days.

0: 10 business days is the notice if the dispute settles before an EDO issues.
2: 30 business days is the deadline to institute a settlement procedure.

q: A title company holds the deposit in a failed sale and both buyer and seller demand it. Which statement is correct?
c: The broker must notify the FREC and request an escrow disbursement order
No escrow disbursement order is available, because the broker does not hold the funds
The broker must have the title company move the deposit into the brokerage's account
The broker must instruct the title company to release the deposit to the seller
ex: An escrow disbursement order is available only when the broker holds the funds. When a title company or attorney holds the deposit, the FREC notice-and-procedure rule does not apply to the broker.

0: An EDO requires the funds to be in the broker's escrow account.
2: The broker has no authority to take the funds from the title company.
3: The broker cannot decide the dispute.

q: A buyer under a contract with a financing contingency applies in good faith but is denied a loan. The broker holds the deposit. What may the broker do?
c: Return the deposit to the buyer without notifying the FREC
Notify the FREC within 15 business days and request an EDO
Hold the deposit until the seller signs a release
Give the deposit to the seller as liquidated damages
ex: Under s. 475.25(1)(d)1, if the buyer in good faith fails to satisfy the financing clause, the licensee may return the deposit without notifying the commission or starting a settlement procedure. The same applies to a condo buyer cancelling under s. 718.503.

1: This is one of the statutory exceptions; no FREC notice is required.
2: The statute allows return to the buyer in this case.
3: A good-faith financing failure is not a buyer default.

q: If the parties choose mediation for an escrow dispute, it must be completed within how many days after the last demand?
ex: Mediation must be completed within 90 days after the last demand; otherwise the broker must promptly use another procedure.

0: 30 business days is the deadline to institute a procedure.

q: An advertisement for a listed property that does not include the brokerage firm's registered name is a:
c: lawful ad if the associate's phone number appears
ex: Omitting the registered brokerage name makes it a blind ad, in any medium.

2: The brokerage name is required regardless of other contact information.

q: A homeowner (not a licensee) posts her own house for sale on social media with her phone number. Must the ad include a brokerage name?
c: Yes, every real estate advertisement must include a brokerage name
No, an owner advertising her own property has no brokerage to name
Yes, unless the asking price is under $500,000, when owners are exempt
Only if she plans to pay a commission to a buyer's broker at closing
ex: Advertising rules for brokerage names apply to licensees' ads. An owner selling her own property is exempt from licensure and there is no brokerage to name.

0: The rule applies to licensee advertising.
3: Paying a commission later does not change who placed this ad.

q: A sales associate posts a listing video on her personal Instagram with her name and phone number, but not her brokerage's name. Which is correct?
c: Lawful because it is her personal account
Lawful if the brokerage name is in her profile page one click away
A blind ad; the registered brokerage name must appear in the ad
Lawful if the seller approved it
ex: Licensee advertising on any medium must include the registered brokerage name. A personal account is not an exception.

0: Personal social media is still advertising by a licensee.
1: The firm name must appear in the ad itself.
3: Seller approval does not cure a blind ad.

q: The entrance sign of a broker's office must include the broker's name, the trade name (if any), and the words:
c: 'Licensed Real Estate Broker' (or 'Lic. Real Estate Broker')
ex: The sign must show the broker's name, any trade name, and 'Licensed Real Estate Broker' or 'Lic. Real Estate Broker'.

3: This is not the required wording.

q: A seller is so happy with the sale that she hands the sales associate a $500 gift card at closing. Which is correct?
c: Lawful, because a voluntary gift after closing is not a commission
Lawful, as long as the gift is worth less than $1,000 and is disclosed
A violation: she may be compensated only by her employing broker
Lawful, if the gift card is disclosed on the closing statement
ex: A sales associate may accept compensation for real estate services only from her employing broker.

0: Anything of value for services is compensation.
3: Disclosure does not fix the payment path.

q: Which payment is lawful?
c: A broker pays an unlicensed assistant $100 for each closed transaction
A broker rebates part of the commission to the buyer, with full disclosure to all parties
A sales associate pays a referral fee directly to a licensee at another brokerage
A broker pays a past customer $300 for each new client referred
ex: A broker may rebate part of the commission to a party to the transaction with disclosure. Payments to unlicensed persons for real estate services are unlawful; an associate cannot pay or receive compensation except through the broker.

0: Per-closing pay to an unlicensed person is compensation for real estate services.
2: Compensation must flow through the employing broker.
3: Paying unlicensed persons for referrals of business is not allowed.

q: A prospective tenant paid $200 for a rental list but did not obtain a rental. She demands a refund within 30 days. How much must be returned (the list was accurate)?
ex: If no rental is obtained, the tenant gets back any amount over 25% of the fee: 75% × $200 = $150. If the list was inaccurate, the full fee is refundable.

0: A refund is required when no rental is obtained.
1: $50 is the 25% the broker may keep.
3: The full fee is refundable only if the information was inaccurate.

q: At a local association meeting, two brokers agree that neither will accept listings below 6%. This is:
c: price fixing, a violation of antitrust law
ex: Commission rates must be negotiated between each broker and client. Agreements between competitors to set rates are price fixing.

0: A written agreement to fix prices is still illegal.
2: There is no lawful 'customary' or 'standard' rate.

q: Which step comes immediately after the DBPR completes its investigation of a complaint?
c: The FREC issues a final order
A probable cause panel decides whether probable cause exists
The licensee appeals to the District Court of Appeal
A formal hearing before an administrative law judge
ex: Complaint → investigation → probable cause determination → formal complaint → hearing → final order → appeal.

0: The final order comes after a hearing.
3: A formal hearing follows the formal complaint.

q: A licensee disputes the facts in the formal complaint. Where is the case heard?
c: Informal hearing before the members of the FREC
Formal hearing before an administrative law judge
Trial before the Florida Supreme Court
Jury trial in the county court where he lives
ex: Disputed facts go to a formal hearing before an administrative law judge, who issues a recommended order. Undisputed facts can be handled at an informal hearing before the FREC.

0: Informal hearings are for undisputed facts.
2: Appeals go to a District Court of Appeal.
3: County courts do not conduct license discipline hearings.

q: A licensee may appeal an FREC final order to the District Court of Appeal within:
ex: Appeal within 30 days of the final order.

q: The maximum administrative fine the FREC may impose per violation is:
ex: Up to $5,000 per violation (count).

q: Performing real estate services for compensation without a license is a:
ex: Operating without a valid, current, active license is a third-degree felony.

0: Most other s. 475.42 violations are second-degree misdemeanors.
1: Rental-list fraud (s. 475.453) has been a first-degree misdemeanor.

q: A licensee repeatedly ignores escrow rules because 'deals always close anyway'. This reckless indifference is best described as:
ex: Culpable negligence is reckless indifference to others' rights, more than a careless mistake.

0: Repeated, knowing disregard goes beyond simple negligence.
3: A false promise is a promise to induce action that the licensee does not intend or cannot keep.

q: How long must a broker keep transaction records and escrow records?
ex: At least 5 years (and at least 2 years after any related litigation ends).

0: 2 years relates to litigation, added after it ends.

q: A licensee tells a buyer, 'The county will never allow anything to be built on that empty lot behind you,' knowing there is no such rule, to close the sale. This is best described as:
c: lawful sales talk to close the deal
ex: Stating a false fact to induce a sale is misrepresentation; framed as an assurance about the future, it is a false promise. Puffing is exaggerated opinion ('best view in town').

0: Puffing is opinion, not a false statement of fact.
3: False statements of fact are violations.

q: The maximum the Real Estate Recovery Fund will pay for claims arising from one transaction is:
ex: $50,000 per transaction (all claimants combined); $150,000 aggregate against one licensee.

q: A sales associate wins a judgment against her former broker for unpaid commissions but cannot collect. May she recover from the Fund?
c: Yes, up to $50,000, because the judgment arose from a real estate transaction
Yes, up to $150,000, the maximum the Fund pays against any one licensee
No; a licensee who acted as a licensee cannot recover for a commission dispute
Only if the broker has filed for bankruptcy and the judgment is discharged
ex: The Fund protects the public. A licensee who acted as a licensee in the transaction (e.g., over a commission) cannot recover.

0: Commission disputes between licensees are excluded.
1: $150,000 is the per-licensee aggregate cap; she is excluded anyway.

q: When the Fund pays a claim based on a judgment against a licensee, the licensee's license is:
c: revoked permanently, with no possibility of reinstatement
automatically suspended until the Fund is repaid with interest
unaffected, because the Fund exists to pay such judgments
placed on probation for 1 year while the licensee repays the Fund
ex: Payment from the Fund automatically suspends the license until the licensee repays the full amount plus interest.

0: It is a suspension, not revocation.
3: Probation is not the automatic result.

q: Which protected classes were added to the federal Fair Housing Act in 1988?
ex: 1988 added familial status and handicap (disability). Sex was added in 1974.

0: Sex was added in 1974; religion was original (1968).
2: Age and marital status are ECOA classes.
3: Race and color were in the original 1968 act.

q: A licensee shows a Hispanic buyer only homes in neighbourhoods where many Hispanic families live, although she did not ask for that. This is:
ex: Steering is directing buyers toward or away from areas based on a protected class.

0: Blockbusting is scaring owners into selling.
1: Redlining is lender discrimination by area.

q: An owner of three single-family homes sells one without a broker but runs an ad saying 'No children'. Which is correct?
c: Exempt, because he owns no more than three single-family homes
Not exempt: discriminatory advertising removes the exemption
Exempt because familial status is not protected
Exempt only if he lives in the house
ex: The single-family owner exemption is lost if a broker is used or a discriminatory advertisement is published.

0: The exemption requires no broker AND no discriminatory advertising.
2: Familial status has been protected since 1988.
3: Owner occupancy is a condition of the Mrs. Murphy exemption, not this one.

q: Which basis of discrimination has NO exemptions under federal law?
ex: The Civil Rights Act of 1866 prohibits racial discrimination in all property transactions without exception.

0: Religious organizations have a limited exemption.
1: Housing for older persons is an exemption.

q: A tenant who uses a wheelchair asks to install grab bars in the bathroom at her own expense. The landlord must generally allow this as a:
ex: A physical change to the unit is a reasonable modification (generally at the tenant's expense). A change in rules or policies is an accommodation.

0: Accommodation is a change in rules or policies.
2: Nonconforming use is a zoning term.
3: A variance is a zoning term.

q: A wheelchair ramp is required at a brokerage's office entrance. Which law governs?
ex: The ADA governs accessibility of public accommodations and commercial facilities, such as a brokerage office.

0: The Fair Housing Act governs housing.

q: Which call to a number on the National Do Not Call Registry is permitted?
c: Calling an expired listing of another brokerage
Calling a customer who closed a purchase with you 14 months ago
Calling someone who inquired about a listing 6 months ago
Calling a FSBO seller you have never met
ex: An established business relationship lasts 18 months after a transaction and 3 months after an inquiry.

0: You have no business relationship with another brokerage's expired listing.
2: An inquiry creates a relationship for only 3 months.

q: Under ECOA, a lender may NOT deny credit because the applicant:
c: has insufficient income to repay the loan
has a poor history of paying debts on time
lacks funds for the required down payment
ex: ECOA prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age, or receipt of public assistance income.

0: Insufficient income is a legitimate credit factor.
2: Payment history is a legitimate factor.
3: Lack of funds is a legitimate factor.

q: The Closing Disclosure must be received by the borrower at least how long before closing?
ex: At least 3 business days before closing (consummation). The Loan Estimate is due within 3 business days of application.

3: 10 days is the lead-paint inspection window.

q: A buyer closes on a purchase-money mortgage for her new home and wants to cancel the loan 2 days later. Which is correct?
c: She may rescind within 3 business days under TILA
She has no TILA right of rescission on a purchase loan
She may rescind only if the APR was disclosed late
ex: TILA's 3-business-day right of rescission applies to refinances and home-equity loans on a principal residence, not to purchase loans.

0: Rescission applies to refinance/home-equity loans, not purchase loans.
3: Late disclosures do not create rescission for purchase loans.

q: Which phrase in an advertisement is a TILA trigger term requiring full credit disclosure?
ex: A specific down-payment amount is a trigger term. General phrases like 'easy financing' or 'low monthly payments' are not.

0: General statements are not trigger terms.
3: This is not a specific credit term.

q: Under RESPA, a title company pays a sales associate $100 for every buyer she refers. This is:
c: lawful, as long as it is disclosed to the buyer in writing
a prohibited kickback for referral of settlement services
lawful, as long as the total stays under $500 per year
lawful, because title insurance is not a mortgage loan
ex: RESPA prohibits kickbacks and unearned fees for referrals of settlement services in federally related residential transactions.

0: Chapter 475 talks about disclosure; RESPA prohibits the kickback outright.

q: A landlord intends to keep part of a tenant's security deposit. Within how many days after the tenant moves out must the landlord send notice by certified mail?
ex: Return within 15 days if no claim; send certified-mail notice of a claim within 30 days; the tenant has 15 days to object.

1: 15 days is the return deadline when no claim is made, and the tenant's objection window.

q: Under current s. 83.57, how much written notice is required to end a month-to-month tenancy that has no specific term?
ex: Current law: month-to-month and quarter-to-quarter 30 days; year-to-year 60 days; week-to-week 7 days. (Older texts said 15 days for month-to-month.)

1: 15 days is the pre-change rule found in older books.

q: A landlord forgets to send the notice of claim and sends it 35 days after the tenant left. What is the result?
c: The claim is still valid, because the damage to the unit is real
The landlord forfeits the right to impose a claim on the deposit
The landlord may keep half of the deposit as a late-notice penalty
The tenant must still object within 15 days or lose the deposit
ex: A landlord who fails to give the 30-day notice forfeits the right to impose a claim on the deposit.

0: Missing the deadline forfeits the claim against the deposit.
3: The objection window matters only if the notice was timely.

q: Which estate gives the greatest bundle of ownership rights?
ex: Fee simple absolute is the most complete ownership: inheritable, unconditional, and of unlimited duration.

0: A life estate ends at death.
1: A defeasible fee can be lost if a condition occurs.
3: An estate for years is a leasehold, not ownership.

q: Ana deeds her house 'to Bruno for life, then to Carla.' Bruno dies. Who owns the house?
ex: When the future interest goes to a third party it is a remainder; Carla is the remainderman. If it returned to Ana it would be a reversion.

0: Reversion applies when no remainderman is named.
1: A life estate cannot be inherited; it ends at Bruno's death.
3: Escheat applies only when no heirs or will exist.

q: A life tenant cuts down all the valuable timber on the property and sells it. This is:
ex: A life tenant must not commit waste — actions that permanently damage the value of the future interest.

0: The life tenant may use but not destroy the property's value.
2: Adverse possession is acquiring another's land.
3: An easement is a right of use.

q: Which is NOT one of the rights in the bundle of rights?
ex: The bundle: possession, control, enjoyment, exclusion, disposition. Escheat is a government power over property of owners who die without will or heirs.

q: A lease for 6 months with a definite end date is an:
ex: Any lease with a definite beginning and end, even shorter than a year, is an estate for years. It ends automatically without notice.

1: A tenancy at will has no fixed term.
2: A periodic tenancy renews period to period.
3: Sufferance is a holdover without consent.

q: With 14 months left on her 3-year lease, a tenant transfers all 14 remaining months to a friend, who pays the landlord directly. This is:
ex: Transferring the entire remaining term is an assignment, even if it is only part of the original term.

0: A sublease transfers only part of what remains.
2: A novation would release the original tenant by agreement with the landlord; nothing says that happened.

q: A retail store pays base rent plus 4% of gross sales over $500,000. This is a:
ex: Rent based on a percentage of the tenant's gross sales is a percentage lease, common in retail.

0: A gross lease has fixed rent with the landlord paying expenses.
1: A net lease shifts property expenses to the tenant.
3: A graduated lease has scheduled rent increases.

q: A commercial tenant pays rent plus property taxes, insurance and maintenance. This is a:
ex: Triple net: the tenant pays taxes, insurance and maintenance in addition to rent.

0: In a gross lease the landlord pays those expenses.
2: A graduated lease has scheduled rent increases.
3: An index lease ties rent to an index such as CPI.

q: Two unmarried friends receive a deed that says nothing about how they hold title. In Florida they own as:
c: joint tenants with right of survivorship
ex: Florida presumes tenancy in common for unmarried co-owners unless survivorship is expressly stated.

0: Florida requires express survivorship language for joint tenancy.
3: Florida is not a community-property state.

q: Ana and Rui own a duplex as tenants in common, 60%/40%. Rui dies with a will leaving everything to his sister. Who owns Rui's 40%?
ex: A tenant in common's share passes by will or to heirs; there is no survivorship.

0: Survivorship belongs to joint tenancy and entireties, not tenancy in common.
2: Escheat applies only without a will or heirs.

q: The four unities required for a joint tenancy are:
ex: PITT: Possession, Interest, Time, Title.

1: Income and tax are not unities.
3: Insurance and transfer are not unities.

q: A creditor obtains a judgment against the husband alone. The couple owns their condo as tenants by the entireties. Can the creditor force a sale of the condo to satisfy the husband's debt?
c: Yes, by forcing a sale of the husband's half of the condo
Yes, by forcing a sale of the entire condo to pay the debt
No, entireties property is shielded from one spouse's individual creditors
Only after the wife dies and the husband becomes the sole owner of the condo
ex: Tenancy by the entireties property is protected from the creditors of only one spouse.

0: Neither spouse holds a separate half.
1: Individual creditors cannot reach entireties property.
3: If the wife dies first, she owns it alone by survivorship and the husband's creditor still cannot reach it.

q: Florida's constitutional homestead protection inside a municipality covers up to:
ex: 1/2 acre of contiguous land within a municipality; 160 contiguous acres outside a municipality.

q: Which claim can result in a forced sale of a Florida homestead?
ex: Homestead protection does not stop property taxes and assessments, the mortgage on the home, or liens for work on the home.

0: General creditors cannot force the sale of homestead.
1: General creditors cannot force the sale of homestead.
3: General creditors cannot force the sale of homestead.

q: A married homeowner holds title to the homestead in his name only and wants to mortgage it. What is required?
c: Only his signature, because title is in his name
His spouse must join in the mortgage
Nothing, if the loan is under $100,000
ex: When the owner is married, the spouse must join in any conveyance or mortgage of the homestead.

0: Homestead rules require spousal joinder regardless of title.
2: Court approval is not the requirement.

q: The buyer of a cooperative apartment receives:
c: shares in the corporation and a proprietary lease
an undivided interest in common elements only
ex: In a cooperative, the corporation owns the building. The buyer receives shares and a proprietary lease, which is personal property.

0: A deed to a unit is a condominium purchase.
3: Common elements belong to condominium ownership.

q: A buyer signs a contract to buy a new condominium unit from the developer. The buyer may cancel within:
ex: Developer sales: 15 days after signing and receiving the required documents. Timeshares: 10 days. Resales: see the flagged resale rule (3 business days in older texts; 7 days in the 2025 statute text).

0: 3 business days is the older resale rule.

q: A timeshare purchaser's statutory cancellation period is:
ex: 10 days, and the right cannot be waived.

3: 15 days is the developer condo rule.

q: A condominium is legally created by:
c: filing articles of incorporation for the association
the first sale of a unit
ex: Recording the declaration of condominium creates the condominium.

1: The association is created separately; the declaration creates the condominium.
2: A CO allows occupancy of a building.

q: In Florida, adverse possession requires open, notorious, hostile and continuous possession for:
c: 5 years, plus a recorded claim of ownership
7 years, plus color of title or payment of taxes
20 years of possession, with no other condition
10 years, plus a survey filed with the county
ex: Florida: 7 years plus either color of title or payment of property taxes. 20 years is the prescriptive easement period.

0: It is 7 years plus color of title or payment of taxes.
2: 20 years is for an easement by prescription.
3: It is 7 years and an additional condition applies.

q: A person dies without a will and without heirs. The property passes to the state by:
ex: Escheat transfers property to the state when there is no will and no heirs.

0: Eminent domain is a taking with compensation.
2: Adverse possession requires possession by a claimant.
3: Devise is a gift of real property by will.

q: Real property left to a person in a will is called a:
ex: A devise is a gift of real property by will; the recipient is the devisee.

0: A bequest is a gift of personal property.
2: Descent is transfer without a will.

q: Which deed gives the buyer the most protection?
ex: A general warranty deed warrants title against defects from any time, even before the grantor owned the property.

1: Special warranty covers only the grantor's period of ownership.
3: Bargain and sale implies ownership but gives no warranties.

q: Which is required for a deed to be valid in Florida?
c: The grantee's signature on the deed at closing
Recording in the county's official public records
Delivery and acceptance during the grantor's lifetime
A notary's acknowledgment of the grantor's signature
ex: A valid deed needs a competent grantor, an identifiable grantee, consideration, words of conveyance, a legal description, the grantor's signature with two witnesses, and delivery and acceptance. Recording and acknowledgment protect against third parties; the grantee does not sign.

0: The grantee does not sign the deed.
1: Recording gives constructive notice; it is not needed for validity.
3: Acknowledgment is needed to record, not for validity.

q: To remove an ex-spouse's possible claim from a title, the ex-spouse would most likely sign a:
ex: A quitclaim conveys whatever interest the grantor may have, without warranties — the standard tool to cure a cloud on title.

0: The ex-spouse would not warrant the entire title.
2: Warranties are unnecessary to release a claim.
3: A deed of trust is a security instrument.

q: How many witnesses must sign a Florida deed with the grantor?
ex: The grantor signs in the presence of two subscribing witnesses (s. 689.01). Leases no longer require witnesses.

0: No witnesses is the current rule for leases, not deeds.

q: A buyer fails to check the public records and later claims she did not know of a recorded easement. Which is correct?
c: She is not bound because she had no actual notice
She is bound because recording gives constructive notice
She is bound only if the seller told her
ex: Recorded documents give constructive notice to everyone, whether or not they read them.

0: Constructive notice applies regardless of actual knowledge.
3: A recorded easement does not void the sale.

q: An owner's title insurance policy protects the owner against:
c: liens and judgments the owner allows to attach after closing
undiscovered defects that existed before the policy date
zoning changes that reduce the property's value after closing
physical damage to the home from hurricanes and flooding
ex: Title insurance covers defects existing before the policy date. It does not cover problems the owner creates later or physical damage.

2: Zoning changes are not title defects.

q: A property is foreclosed. It has a first mortgage recorded in 2010, a judgment lien recorded in 2018, and unpaid property taxes for last year. Which is paid first from the sale?
ex: Property tax and special assessment liens have priority over other liens regardless of recording date. Others follow recording order.

0: Taxes come before even an older first mortgage.
1: A judgment lien is behind taxes and earlier-recorded liens.
3: Liens are paid in priority order.

q: A power company's right to run lines across a property is an easement:
ex: An easement in gross benefits a person or company, not an adjoining parcel; there is no dominant estate.

0: Appurtenant easements benefit a neighbouring parcel.
2: Easements by necessity arise for landlocked parcels.
3: Prescription is acquired by long adverse use.

q: In Florida an easement by prescription requires continuous, open, adverse use for:
ex: 20 years for a prescriptive easement; 7 years (with color of title or taxes) for adverse possession of title.

q: A neighbour's fence extends 2 feet onto your client's lot. This is an:
ex: An encroachment is a physical intrusion onto another's land, typically revealed by a survey.

0: An easement is a right to use land.
3: An appurtenance is a right attached to land.

q: Which is a general lien?
ex: A judgment lien attaches to all the debtor's property in the county where recorded — a general lien. The others are specific liens on one property.

0: A mortgage is a specific lien.
1: A property tax lien is specific to that parcel.
3: A construction lien is specific to the improved property.

q: A restaurant tenant bolted its pizza ovens to the floor. The lease ends and the building is sold. Who owns the ovens?
c: The landlord, because the ovens are bolted to the floor
The building buyer, because fixtures pass with the deed
The tenant, as trade fixtures removed by the end of the lease
The county, as unclaimed property after the lease ends
ex: Trade fixtures installed by a business tenant remain the tenant's personal property and must be removed by the end of the lease.

0: Attachment alone does not decide; trade fixtures stay with the tenant.
1: The buyer acquires the landlord's interest, not the tenant's trade fixtures.

q: A hurricane suddenly moves a river channel. The boundary:
c: moves only if the owner records a new survey
ex: A sudden change is avulsion; boundaries do not move. Gradual changes (accretion/erosion) do move them.

2: A survey does not change the legal rule.
3: The land does not become state land.

q: Rights of an owner whose land borders the Atlantic Ocean are:
ex: Littoral rights apply to oceans, seas and large lakes; riparian rights to rivers and streams.

0: Riparian refers to rivers and streams.
2: Prior appropriation is a western-states doctrine.
3: Air rights concern the space above land.

q: Which legal description must begin and end at the same point?
ex: A metes-and-bounds description starts at the point of beginning and returns to it.

0: Lot and block refers to a recorded plat.
1: Government survey uses townships and sections.
3: A street address is not a legal description.

q: Florida's principal meridian and base line intersect in:
ex: They intersect in Tallahassee.

q: Most homes in platted urban subdivisions are described by:
ex: Lot and block numbers on a recorded plat describe most subdivided urban property.

0: Metes and bounds is common for irregular parcels.
2: Government survey is used for larger rural tracts.
3: Addresses and folio numbers are not legal descriptions.

q: How many acres are in the NW 1/4 of the SE 1/4 of a section?
ex: Multiply the denominators (4 × 4 = 16) and divide 640 by 16 = 40.

q: How many acres are in 'the N 1/2 of the NW 1/4 AND the SW 1/4' of a section?
ex: Compute each parcel separately and add when the description uses AND.

q: Section 1 of a township is located in which corner?
ex: Sections are numbered 1–36 starting in the northeast corner, moving west then back east in a serpentine pattern; section 36 is in the southeast.

0: Section 6 is in the northwest corner.
2: Section 31 is in the southwest corner.
3: Section 36 is in the southeast corner.

q: A rectangular lot measures 330 feet by 660 feet. How many acres is it?
ex: Square feet ÷ 43,560 = acres.

q: A buyer pays $3,000 per acre for the S 1/2 of the NE 1/4 of the SW 1/4 of a section. What is the price?
ex: Find the acreage first, then multiply by the price per acre.

q: Which is NOT an essential element of a valid contract?
ex: Essentials: competent parties, offer and acceptance, legal purpose, consideration. Earnest money is customary but not legally required; mutual promises are sufficient consideration.

q: A contract signed by a 16-year-old to buy land is:
ex: A minor's contract is voidable at the minor's option.

0: Void means no contract at all (e.g., illegal purpose).
2: Unenforceable describes, for example, a contract lacking a required writing.

q: In Florida, an action on a written contract must be brought within:
ex: Written contracts: 5 years. Oral contracts: 4 years.

q: Buyer and seller agree orally on the sale of a house and shake hands. The buyer gives a $5,000 check. Is the agreement enforceable?
c: Yes, because the buyer's check is a signed writing that satisfies the law
Yes, because consideration of $5,000 was paid and accepted by the seller
No, a sale of real property requires a writing signed by the party to be charged
Yes, as long as two witnesses saw the parties agree and shake hands
ex: The statute of frauds requires contracts for the sale of real property to be in writing and signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought.

0: The buyer's check is not the seller's signed agreement.
1: Consideration does not replace the writing requirement.
3: Witnesses do not satisfy the statute of frauds.

q: A signed sale contract where closing has not yet occurred is:
ex: Promises on both sides (bilateral) with obligations still to perform (executory).

0: It is not yet performed, and both parties made promises.
2: It is not yet fully performed.

q: Buyer offers $400,000. Seller counteroffers at $420,000. Buyer rejects the counteroffer. Seller then signs the buyer's original $400,000 offer. Is there a contract?
c: Yes, at $400,000, the price the seller accepted
Yes, at $420,000, the seller's counteroffer price
No, the counteroffer terminated the original offer
Yes, if the seller signed within 24 hours of the offer
ex: A counteroffer rejects and terminates the original offer. After the buyer rejected the counteroffer, nothing remained to accept.

0: The original offer died with the counteroffer.

q: In an option contract, which party is bound to perform if the option is exercised?
c: Both, from the moment the option is signed
ex: The optionor (owner) is bound to sell on the stated terms; the optionee may choose whether to exercise.

0: The optionee has the choice, not the obligation.
2: The option is unilateral until exercised.

q: Between signing the sale contract and closing, the buyer holds:
ex: The buyer has equitable title; legal title passes by delivery of the deed at closing.

q: A seller refuses to close. The buyer asks the court to order the seller to convey the property. This remedy is:
ex: Specific performance orders the breaching party to perform; it is available because each parcel of land is unique.

1: Liquidated damages are pre-agreed money damages.
3: Novation substitutes a party or obligation.

q: Under an exclusive-agency listing, the seller finds a buyer herself with no help from the broker. Is a commission owed?
c: Only if the buyer saw the broker's sign
ex: An exclusive-agency listing lets the owner sell personally without paying a commission. Under exclusive right of sale, the commission would be owed.

3: Only procuring-cause analysis matters if a broker was involved.

q: Which clause is NOT allowed in a Florida written listing agreement?
ex: Written listings must have a definite expiration date and may not contain automatic renewal; a copy goes to the seller within 24 hours.

0: A definite expiration date is required.
2: The commission is an ordinary term.
3: The price is an ordinary term.

q: After a seller signs a written listing agreement, a copy must be given to the seller within:
ex: Within 24 hours.

1: 3 business days is the broker's escrow deposit deadline.

q: A listing in which the broker keeps any amount received above a set price for the seller is a(n):
ex: A net listing pays the broker the excess over the seller's net. It is legal in Florida per the manual but creates conflicts of interest.

0: An open listing is given to several brokers.
2: Exclusive agency is about who may sell.
3: An option listing gives the broker an option to buy.

q: The federal lead-based paint disclosure applies to housing built before:
ex: Pre-1978 housing. 1968 is the Fair Housing Act; 1988 the amendments adding familial status and handicap.

2: 1988 is the Fair Housing Amendments Act.

q: In a Florida sale contract, the 'effective date' is generally the date:
c: the buyer signs and delivers the first written offer to the seller
the last party signs or initials the final offer or counteroffer
of closing, when the deed is delivered and the funds are disbursed
the buyer's escrow deposit clears the bank and is confirmed in writing
ex: Contract deadlines run from the effective date: when the last party signs/initials the final offer or counteroffer.

0: The first offer is not yet a contract.
2: Closing is the end, not the start.
3: Deposit timing is a separate deadline.

q: Under s. 689.302, the seller of residential property must give the buyer a flood disclosure:
c: only if the home lies in a FEMA special flood hazard area
at or before the time the sales contract is executed
within 10 days after closing, with the recorded deed
only if the buyer requests it in writing before closing
ex: The statute requires the flood disclosure form at or before contract execution, covering flood insurance, claims, federal assistance and known flooding. (Added by a 2024 law; not in older textbooks.)

0: The disclosure is not limited to flood zones.
2: It is at or before contract.

q: Florida's radon gas disclosure must appear:
c: only in contracts for homes built before 1978
in contracts for the sale or rental of any building
only when radon has been detected
ex: Florida requires a radon notice at or before contract for the sale or rental of any building.

3: It is a general notice, not triggered by testing.

q: In a mortgage loan, the mortgagor is the:
ex: The mortgagor gives the mortgage (the borrower); the mortgagee receives it (the lender). '-or gives, -ee receives'.

2: The title company is not a party to the mortgage.
